question: How do I trace a custom multi-turn agent in Python?
answer:
Use the Weave agent-tracing API: open a conversation with `weave.start_conversation()`, open one turn per user message with `weave.start_turn()`, and wrap each model call and tool call in `weave.start_llm()` and `weave.start_tool()`. Traces then appear in the **Agents** tab [S1]. This is separate from tracing functions with `@weave.op`, which is a different workflow [S1].

**Steps**
1. Initialize Weave with `weave.init("TEAM/PROJECT")`. This sets up the OTel exporter that sends agent spans to the Agents view [S5]. The quickstart lists a CoreWeave Forge account and API key, an OpenAI API key, and Python 3.10+ as prerequisites [S3]. The OpenAI key is there for the quickstart's example agent.
2. Open a conversation. `start_conversation()` stamps a `conversation_id` on every child span so turns are grouped. If you pass your own `conversation_id`, keep it stable. Reusing it adds turns to the existing conversation. If you omit it, the SDK generates a UUID [S6].
3. Start a turn for each user message. `start_turn()` creates an `invoke_agent` span that is the root of a new OTel trace. It inherits the active conversation's ID. If no conversation is active, the turn has no `conversation_id` and isn't grouped [S2].
4. Inside the turn, wrap each LLM call in `start_llm()` and each tool execution in `start_tool()` [S4].

**Minimal pattern** (adapted from the quickstart [S4]; `call_model` is a placeholder for your own LLM client call)
```python
import weave
weave.init("TEAM/PROJECT")

def run_turn(history, user_message):
    history.append({"role": "user", "content": user_message})
    with weave.start_turn(user_message=user_message, model="gpt-4o-mini"):
        with weave.start_llm(model="gpt-4o-mini", provider_name="openai") as llm:
            reply = call_model(history)   # placeholder
            llm.output(reply)
        history.append({"role": "assistant", "content": reply})
        return reply

with weave.start_conversation(agent_name="my-agent"):
    history = []
    for q in ["First question", "Follow-up question"]:
        run_turn(history, q)
```

**Notes**
- Tracing only records activity. Your agent must still keep and send its own `history` to the model on each turn. The quickstart does this by appending the user, assistant and tool messages to `history` [S4].
- Use the context-manager (`with`) form in Python. The span closes and is sent at the end of the block, even if an exception occurs [S7].
- Weave stores the active conversation, turn and LLM call in context. A function called inside a block can call `start_llm()` or `start_tool()` without being passed the parent [S7].
- The quickstart also calls `llm.record(usage=weave.Usage(...), response_id=..., response_model=...)` on each LLM call. Its code comment says this sets usage, the priced model, and the response id [S4].

If your agent is built on a supported SDK or harness, the docs point to a separate integration page instead of manual instrumentation [S3].

# Trace your agents

> Use the Weave SDK to instrument multi-turn agentic applications and view them in the Agents tab.

> [!TIP]
>
> **This workflow is also available in CoreWeave Agent Lens.** Agent Lens is the Forge experience built for tracing, monitoring, and analyzing AI agents, with automated insights into agent failures and user intents. It uses the same trace data as Weights & Biases Weave, so the traces you already send appear there with nothing to migrate.
> [See how to do this in Agent Lens](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/agent-lens/tracing/instrument.md).

Learn how to instrument a multi-turn agentic application using the W\&B Weave SDK so that you can view, debug, and evaluate your agent's behavior. This guide is intended for developers who build or integrate agents and want structured visibility into conversations, turns, LLM calls, and tool executions.

The Weave SDK for Agents models the full lifecycle of a multi-turn agent conversation: the agent that owns many conversations, the conversation that groups turns together, each user-agent exchange (turn), the LLM calls within a turn, and the tool executions that an LLM triggers. Traces appear in the **Agents** tab of your Weave project. Each conversation shows a multi-turn timeline with nested tool calls, token usage, and feedback.

Weave is built on [OpenTelemetry (OTel)](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/concepts/), the open standard for distributed tracing. Every turn, LLM call, and tool call emits an OTel *span* (a structured record of one operation). Each span is tagged with [GenAI semantic-convention](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/semconv/gen-ai/) attributes like `gen_ai.agent.name` and `gen_ai.conversation.id`.

If you're tracing individual functions as Ops with the `@weave.op` decorator, see [Trace LLM applications](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/tracking/tracing.md) instead.

> Use the Weave SDK to instrument multi-turn agentic applications and view them in the Agents tab.

> [!TIP]
>
> **This workflow is also available in CoreWeave Agent Lens.** Agent Lens is the Forge experience built for tracing, monitoring, and analyzing AI agents, with automated insights into agent failures and user intents. It uses the same trace data as Weights & Biases Weave, so the traces you already send appear there with nothing to migrate.
> [See how to do this in Agent Lens](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/agent-lens/tracing/instrument.md).

Learn how to instrument a multi-turn agentic application using the W\&B Weave SDK so that you can view, debug, and evaluate your agent's behavior. This guide is intended for developers who build or integrate agents and want structured visibility into conversations, turns, LLM calls, and tool executions.

The Weave SDK for Agents models the full lifecycle of a multi-turn agent conversation: the agent that owns many conversations, the conversation that groups turns together, each user-agent exchange (turn), the LLM calls within a turn, and the tool executions that an LLM triggers. Traces appear in the **Agents** tab of your Weave project. Each conversation shows a multi-turn timeline with nested tool calls, token usage, and feedback.

Weave is built on [OpenTelemetry (OTel)](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/concepts/), the open standard for distributed tracing. Every turn, LLM call, and tool call emits an OTel *span* (a structured record of one operation). Each span is tagged with [GenAI semantic-convention](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/semconv/gen-ai/) attributes like `gen_ai.agent.name` and `gen_ai.conversation.id`.

If you're tracing individual functions as Ops with the `@weave.op` decorator, see [Trace LLM applications](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/tracking/tracing.md) instead.

results.heading: Multi-turn conversations
results.snippet:
## Multi-turn conversations

Bedrock Agents preserve conversation state on the service side when you reuse a `sessionId`. To group multiple turns into a single trace in the Weights & Biases UI, wrap the turns in `weave.thread`:

```python lines theme={"system"}
with weave.thread("support-conversation") as t:
    for prompt in [
        "I can't log in to my account.",
        "I already tried resetting my password.",
    ]:
        ask_agent(prompt, session_id=t.thread_id)
```

Weave displays each turn in the UI as individual rows in the Threads view.

results.heading: <kbd>method</kbd> `get_agent_turns`
results.snippet:
### <kbd>method</kbd> `get_agent_turns`

```python theme={"system"}
get_agent_turns(
    conversation_id: 'str',
    limit: 'int' = 50,
    offset: 'int' = 0,
    include_feedback: 'bool' = False
) → AgentConversationChatRes
```

Get the multi-turn chat view for a conversation.

Each turn corresponds to one trace.

**Args:**

* **`conversation_id`**: The conversation whose turns to fetch.
* **`limit`**: Maximum number of turns to return.
* **`offset`**: Number of most-recent turns to skip (for pagination).
* **`include_feedback`**: If true, include feedback on the messages.

**Returns:**
An `AgentConversationChatRes` with the ordered `turns`.

**Example:**

```python theme={"system"}
client = weave.init("entity/project")
resp = client.get_agent_turns(conversation_id="...", limit=20)
for turn in resp.turns:
     for message in turn.messages:
         print(message.type)
```

Choose which workflow to use based on what you want to observe:

* **Use agent tracing if you're building or running an agent.** This is the right fit if you use a supported agent harness or agent SDK, or if you've built a custom agent that you can instrument yourself.

Use the Weave agent-tracing API: open a conversation with `weave.start_conversation()`, open one turn per user message with `weave.start_turn()`, and wrap each model call and tool call in `weave.start_llm()` and `weave.start_tool()`. Traces then appear in the **Agents** tab [S1]. This is separate from tracing functions with `@weave.op`, which is a different workflow [S1].

**Steps**
1. Initialize Weave with `weave.init("TEAM/PROJECT")`. This sets up the OTel exporter that sends agent spans to the Agents view [S5]. The quickstart needs a CoreWeave Forge account and API key, an OpenAI API key, and Python 3.10+ [S3]. The OpenAI key is for the quickstart's example agent, not for Weave itself.
2. Open a conversation. `start_conversation()` stamps a `conversation_id` on every child span so turns are grouped. If you pass your own `conversation_id`, keep it stable. Reusing it adds turns to the existing conversation. If you omit it, the SDK generates a UUID [S6].
3. Start a turn for each user message. `start_turn()` creates an `invoke_agent` span that is the root of a new OTel trace. It inherits the active conversation's ID. If no conversation is active, the turn has no `conversation_id` and isn't grouped [S2].
4. Inside the turn, wrap each LLM call in `start_llm()` and each tool execution in `start_tool()` [S4].

**Minimal pattern** (adapted from the quickstart [S4]; `call_model` is a placeholder for your own LLM client call)
```python
import weave
weave.init("TEAM/PROJECT")

def run_turn(history, user_message):
    history.append({"role": "user", "content": user_message})
    with weave.start_turn(user_message=user_message, model="gpt-4o-mini"):
        with weave.start_llm(model="gpt-4o-mini", provider_name="openai") as llm:
            reply = call_model(history)   # placeholder
            llm.output(reply)
        history.append({"role": "assistant", "content": reply})
        return reply

with weave.start_conversation(agent_name="my-agent"):
    history = []
    for q in ["First question", "Follow-up question"]:
        run_turn(history, q)
```

**Notes**
- Tracing only records activity. Your agent must still keep and send its own `history` to the model on each turn. The quickstart does this by appending each user, assistant and tool message to `history` [S4].
- Use the context-manager (`with`) form in Python. The span closes and is sent at the end of the block, even if an exception occurs [S7].
- Weave stores the active conversation, turn and LLM call in context. A function called inside a block can call `start_llm()` or `start_tool()` without being passed the parent [S7].
- The quickstart also records token usage on each LLM call, using `llm.record(usage=weave.Usage(...), ...)`, so token counts and cost render [S4].

If your agent is built on a supported SDK or harness, the docs point to a separate integration page instead of manual instrumentation [S3].
